anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

apparatus: 7–9 L. ca. 5 Z. kept as printed dots.
Mostly unrestored or heavily restored Greek; English does not fill gaps.

bible_refs.note: Quoted (restored): Alpha and Omega, first and last, beginning and end.

choices.why: The Apocalypse 'in circulation'; Origen's usual caution of attribution.

pass_a_gloss: And so that the things said may not seem to be an assertion, we also call the Savior himself as witness teaching us to have a division, beginning and first. For in the circulating Apocalypse of John he is saying: I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and last, the beginning and the end. [gap] it is shown the beginning to be taken toward other and the first toward other.
pass_b_english: And so that what is said may not seem a mere assertion, we also call the Savior himself as witness, teaching us to have a distinction between beginning and first. For in the Apocalypse that is current of John he is saying: "I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and last, the beginning and the end." (Revelation 22:13) [...] it is shown that the beginning is taken in one sense and the first in another (Revelation 1:8) (Revelation 21:6).
